adjudicator.title: Adjudicator Guide
adjudicator.description: Adjudicators are trusted entities responsible for determining the outcome of prediction markets. When a market reaches its deadline, the adjudicator submits the final result (YES, NO, or INVALID).

items.0: Monitor markets assigned to you for deadline expiry
items.1: Research and verify the actual outcome of events
items.2: Submit settlement transactions with the correct outcome
items.3: Respond promptly to avoid delayed payouts for traders

adjudicator.warning: Incorrect settlements can be vetoed by the Guardian during the finalization window.

owner.title: Owner Guide
owner.description: The Protocol Owner has administrative control over protocol parameters. This role is typically held by a multisig or DAO to ensure decentralized governance.

items.0: Configure fee parameters (bonding fee, trading fee)
items.1: Set fee distribution ratios (liquidity, LP yield, treasury)
items.2: Adjust graduation multiplier for market maturity
items.3: Emergency pause the protocol if critical issues arise

owner.warning: Changes to protocol parameters affect all markets. Test on testnet before applying to mainnet.

adjudicator.manualDesc: A trusted human (the market creator or a delegated authority) reads the question, verifies the outcome off-chain, and submits the final result. Simplest model — no oracles, no proofs — but requires the resolver to be honest within the trial window.
adjudicator.manualUseCase: Niche / low-volume markets, demos, internal use, markets where automation is overkill
adjudicator.zkOracleDesc: Uses zkTLS to prove that a Web2 API response is authentic and untampered. An attestation step is inserted between resolve and settle — the resolver must provide a cryptographic proof that the off-chain data source returned the claimed result.
adjudicator.zkOracleUseCase: Any market resolved by provable Web2 data — prices, scores, API results
adjudicator.zkRuleDesc: Pure blockchain event resolution. A pause-protocol event is tracked and verified via ZK proofs — if the on-chain condition occurred, resolution proceeds automatically. The most minimum-trust setup possible.
adjudicator.agentDesc: AI agents create and resolve markets via single-agent execution or multi-agent voting. Agents are verified through ERC-8004 attestation and TEE secure enclaves, ensuring tamper-proof autonomous resolution.
adjudicator.agentUseCase: AI agent markets, autonomous market creation and resolution
adjudicator.optimisticDesc: Proposer assertion followed by a dispute window. Requires financial bonds to ensure honesty.

1.desc: The guaranteed minimum value of the pool. Liability is calculated as the cost to pay out the most probable outcome (max shares).
